paragraphs.title: The Lord's Kingship and the Stability of the World

easy.explanation: The LORD is clothed with majesty and strength.
easy.q: What is the LORD clothed with?

easy.explanation: Verse 2 says, "Thy throne is established of old."

answers: It is established so that it cannot be moved
It is covered by the sea
medium.explanation: The verse says, "the world also is stablished, that it cannot be moved."
medium.q: What happens to the world because the LORD reigns?

answers: The LORD has surrounded Himself with water
The LORD has equipped Himself with strength
The LORD has hidden Himself from the world
medium.explanation: The LORD girds Himself with strength, presenting Him as fully prepared and powerful.
medium.q: What does the phrase "wherewith he hath girded himself" mean?

medium.explanation: The phrase "from everlasting" points to the LORD's eternal existence.
medium.q: What does "from everlasting" communicate about the LORD?

challenge.explanation: The clothing imagery presents the LORD as a glorious and powerful king.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by describing the LORD as clothed with majesty and strength?

answers: The stable world is followed by the ancient and everlasting throne
The moving sea is followed by a changing throne
The disappearing world is followed by a temporary throne
challenge.explanation: Verse 1 describes the world as immovable, and verse 2 describes the LORD's throne as established from ancient times.
challenge.q: How do verses 1 and 2 develop the idea of stability?

answers: The world is unstable, but the throne is temporary
The world is established, while the throne is established eternally
The world is eternal, but the throne is newly built
challenge.explanation: Both are described as established, but the throne is especially linked with eternity.
challenge.q: What contrast is suggested between the world and the LORD's throne?

short_answers.question: In your own words, explain how the LORD's kingship is connected with the stability of the world.
short_answers.answer: Because the LORD reigns with majesty and strength, the world is established and cannot be moved.
short_answers.explanation: Verse 1 connects the LORD's reign with the world's firm and stable condition.

paragraphs.title: The Song of the Rivers and the Waves

easy.explanation: Verse 3 repeats that "the floods have lifted up their voice."
easy.q: What have lifted up their voice?

easy.explanation: The verse says, "the floods lift up their waves."
easy.q: What do the floods lift up?

easy.explanation: Verse 4 says, "The LORD on high is mightier than the noise of many waters."
easy.q: Who is mightier than the noise of many waters?

medium.explanation: The repeated description creates an image of loud and powerful waters.
medium.q: What do the lifted voices of the floods suggest?

medium.explanation: The word "mighty" emphasizes the strength of the sea's waves.
medium.q: What does the phrase "mighty waves of the sea" describe?

answers: The waters are greater than the LORD
The LORD is mightier than the waters
The LORD is part of the waters
medium.explanation: The verse clearly declares that the LORD is mightier than the waters and waves.
medium.q: How does verse 4 compare the LORD with the waters?

challenge.explanation: The floods are given a human ability—to lift up their voice.
challenge.q: What literary device is used when the floods are said to lift up their voice?

answers: The intensity and persistence of the waters
challenge.explanation: The repetition draws attention to the force and repeated surge of the floods.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the repetition of "the floods have lifted up"?

answers: The waters are described as powerful, yet the LORD is greater
The waters are described as harmless, yet the LORD is afraid
The sea replaces the LORD as king
challenge.explanation: The comparison first magnifies the power of the waters and then declares the LORD superior to them.
challenge.q: Why is the LORD's greater power especially striking in these verses?

short_answers.question: What main idea is communicated by comparing the LORD with the noise and waves of the sea?
short_answers.answer: Although the waters are loud and mighty, the LORD is even mightier.
short_answers.explanation: Verse 4 uses the power of the waters to highlight the LORD's greater strength.

paragraphs.title: The Faithfulness of the Testimonies and the Holiness of God's House

easy.explanation: The verse says, "Thy testimonies are very sure."
easy.q: How are the LORD's testimonies described?

easy.explanation: The verse says, "holiness becometh thine house."
The verse ends with "O LORD, for ever."
easy.q: How long is the LORD associated with His house?

answers: They apply only to the sea
medium.explanation: The word "sure" communicates reliability and trustworthiness.
medium.q: What does it mean that the LORD's testimonies are "very sure"?

answers: Holiness is fitting and appropriate for God's house
Holiness belongs only to the waters
medium.explanation: The wording says that holiness is suitable for and fitting in God's house.
medium.q: What does "holiness becometh thine house" mean?

answers: Reliable testimonies and fitting holiness both belong to God's enduring house
The testimonies remove holiness from the house
Holiness causes the testimonies to disappear
medium.explanation: The verse joins the certainty of God's testimonies with the holiness of His house.
medium.q: How are the two parts of the verse connected?

challenge.explanation: The verse presents God's testimonies as trustworthy and His holiness as enduring.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the combination of "very sure" and "for ever"?

answers: Holiness is essential and fitting for God's dwelling
God's house is portrayed as unholy
Holiness belongs only to the rivers
challenge.explanation: The expression presents holiness as a defining and appropriate quality of God's house.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from saying that holiness becomes God's house?

answers: The waters are stronger than the LORD
God's testimonies are trustworthy, and holiness belongs to His house forever
The world is unstable and the throne will fall
challenge.explanation: Verse 5 concludes the psalm by affirming the certainty of God's testimonies and the lasting holiness of His house.

short_answers.question: How does verse 5 describe both God's word and His house?
short_answers.answer: God's testimonies are completely trustworthy, and holiness is fitting for His house forever.
short_answers.explanation: The verse joins the reliability of God's testimonies with the enduring holiness of His house.
